It also states inputTokens is what was billed rather than what was sent, and that missing token counts are filled at the split average.
reason: This is the public scoreboard that currently defines what 'frontier on Roblox' means. It is the single most decision-relevant artifact found in this sweep. Its two benchmarks are already held out of training by project rule (both RobloxQA splits; LuauLeetcode reserved), and that rule stands - the per-question detail shards must not enter training. Use it as the measurement target, not as a corpus.
biggest_implication: The gap between the best public Roblox-specialist fine-tune (60.2) and a general frontier model (91.0) is about 31 points on this board. No existing Roblox fine-tune is near frontier. Today the best Roblox model is a general frontier model, not a Roblox model.

card_admits: States plainly that it is not an official Kwaipilot release; that only epoch 1 shipped; that post-fine-tune RobloxQA numbers for this checkpoint are not published and the 87.60% is the BASE model's score, not this model's; and that it is not intended as a drop-in frontier replacement.
reason: The most useful card in the sweep after the leaderboard. It publishes a complete, per-source, post-dedup row count for a 42,302-row Roblox SFT mix built entirely from public Hugging Face datasets. That is an existence proof, with arithmetic, that tens of thousands of admissible-shaped rows are assemblable from sources we have already triaged - and it tells us what each source actually yields after filtering, which no dataset card does.
conflict_with_project_rule: IMPORTANT: this run trains on RobloxQA-v2.0 TRAIN and holds out only TEST. The Apple rule holds out BOTH RobloxQA splits. Do not copy this mix as-is. Its 4,573 + 2,290 + 2,281 = 9,144 RobloxQA-derived rows are inadmissible here, which reduces its reusable portion to roughly 33,158 rows by its own table.

reason: Already reviewed and rejected in manifests/model-method-reviews.jsonl. This re-read ADDS two facts that strengthen the rejection rather than weaken it: (1) the corpus is tagged literally 'custom' and is not public, so its 28,005 rows are unobtainable and unverifiable; (2) the card names the Drawing API, which is an exploit-client drawing library, not a Roblox engine API - concrete corroboration of the existing 'executor-oriented' finding rather than the card's own vaguer admission. A loss of 0.519 is not capability evidence.

card_admits: States the reward is 60% an LLM judge. Does not claim an external benchmark; every number is from its own scorers.
reason: The scores are self-graded on 50 tasks by a pipeline whose dominant term is the same family of model that wrote the gold answers. That is not capability evidence and must not be cited as one. The METHOD is worth keeping: reverse-labelling raw the-luau-stack files into (task, code) pairs, then best-of-N with a deterministic + judge hybrid. That is a concrete answer to 'how do you get instruction data out of a raw code corpus'.

reason: GGUF quants, LoRA adapters and re-merges of models already in this register. They inherit their upstream's dataset tags, which is why a tag-based search over-counts the field roughly two to one. None is an independent source. Listed by name so a later sweep can skip them by pattern.

Match the word Roblox but are not Luau code models: safety and moderation classifiers, 3D and image generators, avatar/clothing/GFX LoRAs, sentiment and autotrain experiments, roleplay personas, RVC voice models, and repos whose only connection is an owner name containing 'roblox'. Rejected as a class so the next sweep does not re-triage them one by one.
notable_within: The Roblox/* rows are the substantive ones and carry a finding of their own - see the official-org row below. ChatBotExploit/RobloxExploit is named only to mark it as out of bounds, not as a lead.

reason: Roblox publishes no Luau or code-generation model at all. Everything in its model namespace is either trust-and-safety classification (voice, PII, RobloxGuard) or 3D generation (cube3d, cubepart). This is worth stating explicitly because the absence is easy to mistake for a gap in the search: there is no official Roblox code model to benchmark against or learn a recipe from. Whatever Roblox runs behind Assistant, it has not shipped it here.
